doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: His own album, tonight's set and travel plans
summary: He produced an album of originals and has a Dick Hyman concert to rehearse.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Did you mention to me you’d recorded some of your own material recently?

Within the last couple of years, yeah. I did I think seven originals out of twelve on this record I produced. And I wish I’d had a little more money to get a little better sound quality, but I’m funny that way. I’m very happy with it as far as at least having created myself an opportunity to do some writing and get some good musicians to play it — good lesser known musicians except for Duffy Jackson who was the drummer on it. Do you have a copy? I’ll give you one.
I would love to have one for our archive actually.
And you’re on tonight, two or three times?
Once, maybe twice if Jay Leonhart insists.
And you’ve got to leave for home tomorrow?

I’m leaving for home, I’ve got a concert with Dick Hyman, we’ve got a rehearsal with him Tuesday morning at ten o’clock, so I have to leave tomorrow to be able to make it there somewhere in the middle of the night, this is on the west coast to Florida, and probably get six or seven hours of sleep and get up and start rehearsing.
Yeah. Well it probably will be a good one with Dick Hyman.
